metadata.name: Map design — the interview that draws a map
metadata.description: Factory graph 4 (RF-14 to RF-20): somebody describes a problem they keep solving by hand, and this map interviews them into a map of their own. One question per session; every answer re-dispatches the same node with the whole exchange in the prompt; the last session hands back a draft bundle — a graph plus one manifest per node — for a person to register or export. The interview is itself a map, not special code.
metadata.source: written for t360, from §3.3 of the requirements (v2.7)

nodes.description: Asks one question per session and reports the map under construction after every answer. It stays on this node for as long as it has something to ask: a session that asks blocks the job here, and the answer re-dispatches this same node.

job.description: the problem in the person's own words

perguntas_respondidas.description: every question of this interview that already came back

environment.description: the MCP servers this engine reaches, the registered classes that read like this request, and the drafts derived from the skills this person already has

skill_drafts.description: one draft manifest per `SKILL.md` found at the source this person named; empty when they named none

skill_drafts_error.description: why that source could not be read; the interview relays it and moves on

interview.description: this node's own bucket: the draft as the last turn left it, and the skill source an earlier turn named

done.description: false while there is still something to ask; true on the last turn, which asks nothing

draft.description: the whole map as it stands after this turn, never a patch

skill_source.description: where this person's existing skills are, reported once by the turn that asked; a later turn that omits it does not lose it

checks.instruction: Read the session's own output and answer both, quoting the exact text that supports each answer. 1. Does the turn end with AT MOST ONE `input-request` block, and does that block ask exactly one thing — no compound question, no list of decisions? 2. Does the reported draft still carry everything the previous turns settled, plus what this turn's answer added? Name any field that was present before and is missing now.
checks.description: The two ways this node fails silently: asking two things at once, which makes an answer unattributable, and reporting a draft that lost what an earlier turn had already settled.

checks.instruction: Compare the turn's question against the servers this dispatch was given in `environment.mcp_servers`. When the step reaches an external system that none of them covers — and a `null` list covers none — the question's `context` has to carry a line of its own reading `NEEDS_MCP_SERVER: <capability>`; when one of them does cover it, that line must not be there at all. Quote the context and the server list.
checks.description: The screen turns that one line into up to three suggestions from the public MCP registry, so a missing line costs a person the help and a spurious one sends them looking for a server they already have.

checks.instruction: Read the `environment.skill_drafts` this turn was dispatched with and the skill manifests in the draft it reported, and answer both, quoting the exact text that supports each answer. 1. For every reported manifest that clearly started from one of those drafts, do its `input`, `output` and `checks` reflect an answer somebody gave in this interview — rather than the draft's own placeholders (`revisor humano escreve o JSON Schema aqui`) or its derived commands, carried over verbatim? Name any field that is still the draft's. 2. Are that manifest`s `permissions` at or under the safe default the draft arrived with — `filesystem.read` only, `filesystem.write` empty, `network.allowed` false? Quote them.
checks.description: A draft derived from somebody else's `SKILL.md` is a starting point, not an answer. Copied through unchanged it produces a step nobody was asked about — and a permission set nobody approved.

nodes.description: Writes the draft out as a bundle directory, holds it against the graph validator, and reports it as the job's result. It registers nothing: that is a person's decision, at the screen.

interview.description: the interview's own bucket; its LAST turn is the one that survives the merge

bundle.description: the draft written out and checked — what the next step registers or exports

checked.description: what the validator answered, so a person reads a verdict and not a claim

note.description: one line: what the map covers, and anything the interview left rough

checks.description: The draft is held against the same validator that guards the bundles committed in this repository — structure and the four soundness rules. One violation is EXPECTED and is not a defect: `node_with_contract` also asks each node for a pinned `hash`, and a draft has none, because computing the pin belongs to whoever registers (D4). Report it as such; every other violation is a real one.

edges.description: The only edge in the map, and there is no self-loop beside it: asking blocks the job on `interview` itself, and answering re-dispatches that same node. A session that asked nothing is a session that finished interviewing.
